quarterly_data.signal: Roche nine-month 2026 sales (ad hoc announcement / Investor Update, 22 October 2026): Group sales CHF 46,493 million, +6% at constant exchange rates (CER), +1% in CHF and +7% in USD; Q3 sales grew +7% at CER and +8% in CHF as exchange rates stabilised. Pharmaceuticals Division CHF 36,212 million (+7% CER): United States CHF 18,712 million (+5%), Europe CHF 6,819 million (+2%), Japan CHF 2,352 million (+25%, mainly product supply to third parties plus a positive timing effect from a new ERP system) and International CHF 8,329 million (+10%); China stable. The top five growth drivers (Xolair, Hemlibra, Ocrevus, Phesgo, Vabysmo) reached CHF 16.8 billion (+12% CER); sales of products with expired patents fell by CHF 0.4 billion at CER. Top products: Ocrevus CHF 5,317 million (+7%), Hemlibra CHF 3,750 million (+12%), Vabysmo CHF 3,196 million (+10%), Tecentriq CHF 2,615 million (+5%), Xolair CHF 2,521 million (+20%), Phesgo CHF 2,064 million (+18%), Polivy CHF 1,302 million (+24%), Columvi CHF 327 million (+67%), Enspryng CHF 319 million (+28%). Diagnostics Division CHF 10,281 million (+4% CER): Core Lab CHF 5,755 million (+5%), Molecular Lab CHF 1,836 million (+3%), Near Patient Care CHF 1,348 million (-5%), Pathology Lab CHF 1,342 million (+10%); North America +9%, Asia-Pacific -4% on healthcare pricing reforms in China.
quarterly_data.figure: 9M 2026 Group sales CHF 46,493 million (+6% CER); Q3 +7% CER; Pharma CHF 36,212 million (+7%); Diagnostics CHF 10,281 million (+4%)

quarterly_data.signal: Outlook for 2026 confirmed: Roche expects Group sales growth in the mid single digit range (CER), core earnings per share to develop in the high single digit range (CER), and a further dividend increase in Swiss francs. CEO Thomas Schinecker: Roche advanced another five potential new medicines into the final stage of development this year and now aims to bring up to 20 new medicines to patients by 2030; giredestrant is under FDA Priority Review in both early-stage and advanced breast cancer and Roche is 'fully prepared to launch later this year, pending approval'.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 Group sales growth mid single digit (CER); core EPS growth high single digit (CER); up to 20 new medicines by 2030

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 regulatory and diagnostics milestones (Investor Update) not covered by earlier releases: US approval of Gazyva/Gazyvaro for reducing the risk of relapse in patients 2 years of age and older with frequently relapsing or steroid-dependent childhood-onset idiopathic nephrotic syndrome; US FDA clearance of the Elecsys pTau217 blood test (company: the first and only FDA-cleared single-biomarker blood test supporting both rule-in and rule-out assessment of amyloid pathology across primary and specialty care), designed for Roche's installed base of more than 4,500 cobas laboratory instruments in the US; launch of two real-time PCR tests for the US Cyclospora cayetanensis outbreak and delivery of molecular tests supporting the Democratic Republic of the Congo's Ebola response; positive phase II data for petrelintide in overweight or obesity and type 2 diabetes.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 4,500 cobas instruments in the US

quarterly_data.signal: Manufacturing and R&D capacity (Investor Update): Genentech announced a USD 750 million manufacturing expansion in Hillsboro, Oregon for the assembly of injectable medicines and delivery devices, which will double the size of the existing facility and is expected to create an additional 250 specialised manufacturing jobs; Roche also lists a small molecules facility in Basel, Switzerland among its Q3 capacity expansions. These form part of Roche and Genentech's USD 50 billion investment in US manufacturing and R&D.
quarterly_data.figure: Hillsboro expansion approximately USD 750 million; doubles the facility; 250 jobs
